clue.text: Confection best to keep cold

indicators.note: one word is said to keep another when it holds it within its own letters

parts.note: the best of something is the choice of it, the pick
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Advice on storing a dessert: it's wisest to keep it chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHOC ICE is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate-covered ice-cream bar is a sweet treat, a kind of confection.

clue.text: Old English king and James VI both briefly having a picnic, perhaps?

indicators.note: each of the two names is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Alfred the Great was an Anglo-Saxon king of England
James VI was King of Scots, so a Scot

explanation.surface: Two historic monarchs, one English and one Scottish, are imagined eating outdoors together.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of each name leaves ALFRE and SCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating on a rug outside is dining in the open air, the Italian-derived sense of the word; 'perhaps' marks a picnic as just one example.

clue.text: Punk's tender old Indian city

parts.note: Punk is the setter, so 'Punk's' means the setter's own, i.e. my
tender as in painful to the touch means sore

explanation.surface: The setter offers up an old city in India, as if presenting a tender bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore, now officially Mysuru, is a historic city in Karnataka, southern India, so the old name fits.

clue.text: Almost all went wrong in post-Renaissance language

indicators.note: letters that went wrong are put in a mistaken order, so they are rearranged
almost all of the word means drop its final letter

explanation.surface: Nearly everything went awry in some language of the period after the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost all' gives AL; with WENT the letters ALWENT are rearranged to NEWLAT, then IN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The scholarly Latin used from about 1500 onwards, in science and botany, is the form named after the Renaissance.

clue.text: One Olympian about two lengths behind another, last in relay — old performer

indicators.note: the cyclist's name with its insertion comes behind, after, the runner's

parts.note: Zola Budd was a South African-born Olympic distance runner

indicators.note: the last letter in the word relay is taken
about means going round, so the cyclist's name surrounds the two letters

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track cyclist
L is the abbreviation for length, so two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A race report: one Olympic athlete trails another by two lengths, finishing last in the relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Olympian' is the cyclist and 'another' the runner; 'behind' puts the cyclist's part second, as the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock and roll singer of 'Peggy Sue' died in 1959, so he is a performer from long ago.

clue.text: Swine — one bold in action amid conflict

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the other pieces sit inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: letters in action are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A courageous fighter goes into battle, the brave one in the thick of the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' shuffles the letters of bold into LDBO.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild ancestor of the domestic pig is a member of the swine family.

clue.text: Rope in the end holding artist up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: the tail is the end of something, as of a procession
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A rope ends up looped around an artist, holding them aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIL holding RA gives TAIRAL, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso used by cowboys for catching livestock is a long noosed rope.

clue.text: Continue to smile, as Olympian

definitions.meaning: to beam is to smile broadly, and to carry on doing so is to keep beaming
The American long jumper whose 1968 Olympic record stood for decades

explanation.surface: Keep grinning, as an Olympic champion does on the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is an idiom for carrying on smiling; as one it is the surname of the 1968 long-jump champion.

clue.text: See 5
Explain cryptic clue? I see!

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to see someone is to go out with them, to date them

explanation.surface: A solver, stuck on a puzzle, asks for the clue to be explained and then exclaims that they get it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' turns CLUE into ELUC, followed by I and DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear and understandable is to explain it; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: See 24
Artistic movement, stage kept in check

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other, contained by it

parts.note: a dam checks, holds back, the flow of water
a dais is a raised platform or stage

explanation.surface: A theatrical arts trend where the staging was kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: The early twentieth-century anti-art movement of Tzara and Duchamp is a school of art.

clue.text: Old source of music like Punk almost beyond comparison, initially

indicators.note: the remaining pieces go beyond, after, that first letter
initially means the first letter of the word comparison is taken

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Punk is the name of the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: Punk the setter claims to be an incomparable source of music, almost boastfully.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then AS plus SETTE ('almost' SETTER) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape cassettes were a popular format for recorded music before CDs and streaming, so they are an old music medium.

clue.text: Olympian lit up English town

parts.note: Usain Bolt is the Jamaican Olympic sprint champion
a light that is lit up is on

explanation.surface: An Olympic hero lights up a town in England, perhaps with a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a large town in Greater Manchester in the north-west of England.

clue.text: I say, I say, I say?

definitions.text: I say, I say, I say?

parts.words: I say, I say, I say?
parts.note: the music-hall comedian's catchphrase written three times shows I three times, which is how three is written in the ancient Roman system

explanation.surface: The classic opening line of an old music-hall joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the repeated I as a symbol: three Is make III, the Roman way to write three.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters I, V, X and so on are the symbols of the ancient Roman counting system; I stands for one.

clue.text: Man has to air broadcast for artist

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man has to go on air for an artist, as in a radio or TV feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who creates cartoons and moving drawings is an artist working in film.

clue.text: Steps taken backwards, or one giant leap?

definitions.meaning: Michael Jackson's famous dance move glides the feet backwards while seeming to walk forward
Neil Armstrong called his first step on the lunar surface one giant leap for mankind

explanation.surface: A dance move, or the famous line spoken by the first astronaut on the lunar surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the gliding dance step made famous by Michael Jackson, and the 1969 Apollo 11 stroll.

clue.text: General tries to regroup, most suspicious

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

indicators.note: to regroup is to rearrange a group, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A general, after failed attacks, tries to regroup his troops while very wary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being leery means being wary or distrustful, and the superlative is the most distrustful.

clue.text: Olympian flag posted

parts.note: in golf the flag marking the hole is called the pin
a letter that is posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A flag is put up for an Olympic athlete, as at a medal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Matthew Pinsent is a British rower with four Olympic gold medals.

clue.text: Olympian formerly taken by the ultimate in combat sport

indicators.note: the athlete's name is taken by, follows, that single letter
the ultimate, final letter of the word combat is taken

parts.note: Jessica Ennis, the heptathlete, competed under that name before becoming Ennis-Hill

explanation.surface: An athlete once picked up by a combat discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly' points to the heptathlete's maiden name, before marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimbledon's racket-and-ball game is a sport, and is itself an Olympic event.

clue.text: Olympian god exercises

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
PE, physical education, is school exercises

explanation.surface: An Olympian deity working out in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' looks like it means a Greek god; it is a modern athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Thorpe is the Australian swimmer who won five Olympic gold medals.

clue.text: See running water or vapour, then?

definitions.meaning: to see something is to spot or observe it
water that flows or has turned to steam is in neither case frozen, so split as two words it describes something that isn't frozen

explanation.surface: Look at water flowing, or turning to steam.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to spot it, or observe it; the verb means the same.

clue.text: Olympian queen perhaps in Olympian competition, invariably leads

indicators.note: in means the chess piece sits inside the runner's name

parts.note: Seb Coe is a British middle-distance runner and Olympic champion
a queen is one example of a chessman, so man

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A queen takes part in Olympic competition and always leads the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second the runner. A queen is one chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia Comaneci, the Romanian gymnast, scored the first perfect ten at the 1976 Olympics.

clue.text: Out of debt, a small sum of money used to give change

parts.words: small sum of money used to give change
parts.note: a float is the cash kept in a till at the start of trading so change can be given

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper starts out of debt, with a little cash in the till for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solvent, free of debt, is an idiomatic sense of staying above water.

clue.text: Author, part almost stolen by rival of Johnson, Ben?

indicators.note: a piece stolen by another is taken inside it

parts.note: The surname-first style 'Johnson, Ben' tells us to write the rival surname first too

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An author's role gets nearly stolen by a sprinter's rival.
explanation.walkthrough: ROL goes into LEWIS CARL to give the answer. 'Johnson, Ben' looks like the lexicographer Samuel Johnson's friend Ben Jonson but is the Canadian sprinter.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' wrote under this pen name, so he is an author.

clue.text: Shock, as first of runners hampered by loss of power

indicators.note: the letter is hampered, held in, by the word around it

parts.note: an outage is a cut in the electricity supply

indicators.note: the first letter of the word runners is taken

explanation.surface: A race thrown into shock as the leading runners are slowed by a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of shock and anger; as a verb it means to offend greatly.

clue.text: Outdoor kit that is carried by Olympian

indicators.note: a piece carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: Allan Wells was the Scottish sprinter who won the 1980 Olympic 100m
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: An athlete carrying their outdoor gear.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLIES are British for rubber boots, wellingtons.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof rubber boots are footwear worn outside, often in mud and rain.

clue.text: Illustrated issue primarily drowned by tropical storms

indicators.note: a letter drowned by others is submerged within them
storms suggest turmoil, so the letters are rearranged
primarily means the first letter of the word issue

explanation.surface: A news story that tropical storms washed out, with a key issue drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' turns TROPICAL into PICTORAL, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with lots of pictures, like a magazine, is illustrated.

clue.text: Offence taken in wars only

indicators.note: the answer is taken in, contained within, the run of words

explanation.surface: A crime committed only in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.
